review_notes: I read the whole file and the Mathlib Kan-extension API (Pointwise.lean) near pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map. I searched the formal-frontier sources for uses of oldPointwiseModule and pointwiseModule_eq_old. The only hits are in this file, so the old copy has no other users. I could not run Lean, so I did not check that the proposed rewrites compile. In particular, the generic lemma's universe and instance requirements (Category.{v} C, HasColimits C, ConcreteCategory C) are patterned on the existing `pointwiseToPullback` signature. I also noticed `ringGenerator`/`groupGenerator` (lines 102–118) and the two `pointwiseMap_id`/`comp` proofs. I judged those thin wrappers or short routine proofs, so I did not report them.

findings.problem: The two theorems have identical statements and proofs. Both do a `change … ≫ … .hom r = _`, then `erw [Functor.pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map, colimit.ι_desc]`, then `rfl`. The only difference is that one uses the presheaf `R` in `RingCat` and the other uses `M.presheaf` in `AddCommGrpCat`. The real fact is the categorical identity that `colimit.ι` composed with the Kan-extension map along `g` is `colimit.ι` at `(CostructuredArrow.map g).obj i`. That fact does not depend on the target category. Each copy re-proves it and carries its own fragile `erw`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one generic lemma. Take `C : Type (v+1)` with `[Category.{v} C] [HasColimits C]`, `F : Y.Presheaf C`, `g : op U ⟶ op V` and `i : index f U`. Its statement is `colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj (Opens.map f).op (op U) ⋙ F) i ≫ ((Opens.map f).op.pointwiseLeftKanExtension F).map g = colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj (Opens.map f).op (op V) ⋙ F) ((CostructuredArrow.map g).obj i)`. Prove it once by `erw [Functor.pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map, colimit.ι_desc]; rfl`, as in the current bodies. Then `ring_map_ι` is `ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (thatLemma f R g i) r` and `group_map_ι` is `ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (thatLemma f M.presheaf g i) m`. The same pattern is used in `pointwiseMap`'s naturality proof and `pointwiseMap_ι`, so those can reuse the categorical lemma too.
findings.benefit: The non-trivial colimit/Kan-extension unfolding is proved once, in the form Mathlib itself uses in `Pointwise.lean`. The ring and group versions become one-line corollaries. A future change in how `pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map` unfolds then needs one fix, not two.

findings.problem: `pointwiseModule` repeats the whole construction of `oldPointwiseModule`, about 40 lines. The copy re-inlines the `IsFiltered` instance (already given at lines 151–161 of the same file as `meetIndex`, `meetLeft` and `meetRight`) and the `InitiallySmall` instance. It also re-inlines `indexProj`, `indexedRing`, `indexedModule`, `ringIso` and `groupIso` as local `let`s. The final `Module` structure (`AddEquiv.module` followed by `Module.compHom`) is the same. The file itself proves the two are `rfl`-equal in `pointwiseModule_eq_old`. Two copies of the nontrivial transport construction must be kept in sync, and `pointwiseModule_eq_old` exists only to witness the redundancy. A grep of the formal-frontier sources finds no other use of `oldPointwiseModule` or `pointwiseModule_eq_old`.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one body, the helper-based one at lines 130–143. Make the public `pointwiseModule` that body, either by renaming the helper or by `:= oldPointwiseModule f R M U` with the `@[instance_reducible]` attribute. Delete the inlined copy at lines 150–186 and delete `pointwiseModule_eq_old`. The private `IsFiltered` and `InitiallySmall` instances are in scope for this definition. If the public instance must not mention private declarations, make `meetIndex`, `meetLeft`, `meetRight`, `ringIso` and `groupIso` non-private or add the needed `public` exports. I have not compiled this.
findings.benefit: This removes about 60 lines of duplicated construction and the `rfl` bridge theorem. The module structure is then defined in exactly one place, so later changes to the scalar action cannot make the two copies drift apart.

findings.excerpt: obtain ⟨i, a, b, ha, hb⟩ := pointwise_jointly_surjective f R M U r m
findings.problem: Both proofs of 'a map commutes with scalar multiplication' use the same reduction to generators. They get generators from `pointwise_jointly_surjective`, rewrite `r` and `m` with `erw [← ha, ← hb]`, and then rewrite `r • m` as a generator with `erw [← pointwise_smul_ι f R M U i a b]`. Only after that do they apply their own naturality lemmas (`group_map_ι`/`ring_map_ι`, or `pointwiseMap_ι`). The reduction is the same argument in both places, and both depend on fragile `erw` rewrites with instances selected by `letI`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma that packages the generator reduction. For `r` and `m` in the pointwise Kan colimits at `U`, it gives `∃ (i : index f U) (a : R.obj i.left) (b : M.obj i.left), colimit.ι _ i a = r ∧ colimit.ι _ i b = m ∧ pointwiseSmul f R M U r m = colimit.ι _ i (a • b)`. Prove it by `pointwise_jointly_surjective`, then `subst`, then `(pointwiseSmul_eq …)`/`pointwise_smul_ι`. Both theorems then start with `obtain ⟨i, a, b, rfl, rfl, h⟩ := …`. They can use `pointwiseSmul` consistently instead of re-selecting instances with `letI`, and then finish with the one lemma specific to each (the `group_map_ι`/`ring_map_ι` step or `pointwiseMap_ι`). This is a modest refactor. The shared part is the instance-sensitive `erw` setup rather than a long calculation.
findings.benefit: The instance-sensitive rewriting is localized in a single lemma. The two main proofs shrink to the facts specific to each: restriction maps for one, `pointwiseMap` for the other. Any further proofs of 'X commutes with the Kan scalar action' could then reuse it.
